Throttling was caused by enterprise route budget/admission control under regional pressure: Proxima’s chat+embeddings bursts exceeded the conservative burst multiplier / enterprise route budget, so the policy engine returned overload/admission 429s (not mainly billing quota). We applied a time-boxed, region-scoped burst multiplier increase for PROXIMA-ENT-014 on chat+embeddings in us-east with a 14-day expiry and automatic rollback guardrails. To verify it is not burning enterprise route SLOs, monitor the protected-route SLO dashboards: enterprise p99 latency, enterprise availability/error budget burn, shed_rate, admission_control_active, queue depth/scheduler lag, and confirm enterprise overload shedding stays at or below the 0.1% for 10 minutes paging threshold and that p99 latency burn does not trip the rollback threshold.

Procedure:
1) Declare/confirm an incident and identify a known-good prior runtime release tag.
2) Pause the progressive rollout immediately so it cannot advance.
3) Hosted: pin the service to the rollback tag, redeploy the affected regions (non-critical/canary first, then remaining bad regions), then verify 5xx, GPU utilization, TTFT, and token/s recover. Lock the tag to prevent auto-advance.
4) Dedicated: identify impacted clusters/tenants, pin the rollback tag per cluster, redeploy cluster by cluster, and coordinate CS/comms for sensitive tenants.
5) Keep the incident open until stability holds for 30 minutes on Hosted and 60 minutes on Dedicated, and capture job links, affected regions/clusters, timings, metrics, and customer comms.

If using the Redwood tooling runbook specifically: pause rollout, set the tag, deploy, verify 5xx < 0.5% for 10 minutes plus TTFT/gpu_oom_count back to baseline, then lock the tag. For Dedicated, set the tag and deploy per cluster.
